evidence.section: Full-paper method / memory representation and retrieval
evidence.paraphrase: For each streaming video segment, the memorization policy emits an episodic memory conditioned on recent segments and prior memories; evaluation answers using memory alone.
During operation, TaskMem applies LLM-mediated memory editing to temporally ordered event-centric textual memory; the memory state changes while the governing update policy remains fixed.

After deployment, recent environment tasks define preference feedback used to update a lightweight adapter that persistently changes what the memorization policy writes. The persistent later-use effect is deployment-feedback evolution of the reusable write policy.

derived.hybrid_relation: The evaluated memory output is a single textual episodic stream.

adjudication_notes: Strict-tier full-paper review (PDF p. 5): Deployment-time online learning updates a reusable adapter from recent tasks/preferences and changes later memory-writing behavior, satisfying strict T3. The qualifying feedback occurs during deployment/inference and affects later use.
